title: Patient-specific Modeling of the Heart: Estimation of Ventricular Fiber Orientations
protocol: Acquire structural MRI and DTMRI images of a normal adult human heart in diastole.
Extract the ventricular myocardium from the structural image using ImageJ.
Fit closed splines through landmark points placed along epicardial and endocardial boundaries for each short-axis slice manually every 10th slice.
Interpolate landmark points for remaining slices linearly using MATLAB.
Compute primary eigenvectors of the DTs in the DTMRI image to reconstruct fiber orientations.
Acquire an image of the patient heart in diastole using cardiac CT or MRI.
Reconstruct the patient heart geometry from the acquired image.
Resample the patient image prior to reconstruction for a 1 mm² in-plane resolution.
Adjust the number of slices and out-of-plane interpolation interval so that the segmented patient heart image has a slice thickness of 1 mm.

Perform an affine transformation on the atlas ventricular image based on thirteen landmark points: LV apex, two RV insertion points at base, two RV insertion points midway between base and apex, and four sets of two evenly divided RV and LV epicardial contour points.
Deform the affine-transformed atlas ventricles further to match the patient geometry using large deformation diffeomorphic metric mapping (LDDMM).
Morph the DTMRI image of the atlas.
Re-position image voxels according to the transformation matrix of the affine matching.
Re-orientate the DTs according to the deformation field of the LDDMM transformation.
Use the preservation of principal directions (PPD) method for re-orientation of DTs.
Compute the primary eigenvector of the DTs to estimate patient fiber orientations from the morphed atlas DTMRI image.
Acquire ex vivo structural MR and DTMR images of six normal canine hearts.
Generate heart failure in canines via radiofrequency ablation of the left bundle-branch followed by tachypacing at 210 min-1 for three weeks.
Acquire ex vivo structural MR and DTMR images of three failing canine hearts.
Segment ventricles from all canine hearts similarly to the human atlas heart.
Denote ventricles segmented from normal canine hearts as hearts 1 through 6, and those from failing canine hearts as hearts 7 through 9.
Obtain five different estimates of ventricular fiber orientations for heart 1 by using each of hearts 2 to 6 as an atlas.
Estimate fiber orientations for each of the failing ventricles using heart 1 as the atlas.
Compute the estimation error for each data point using |θc-θa|.
Calculate the acute angle between estimated and acquired fiber directions in three-dimensions by means of the vector dot product.
Construct six models from heart 1: one with DTMRI-acquired fiber orientations (model 1) and five with estimated fiber orientations datasets (models 2 to 6).
For each of the three failing heart geometries, construct two ventricular models: one with DTMRI-acquired fiber orientations and the other with estimated fiber orientations.
Construct heart failure models using DTMRI-acquired fibers as models 7 to 9.
Denote heart failure models constructed from estimated fibers as models 10 to 12.
Use monodomain representation in the models to describe cardiac tissue.
Calculate pseudo-ECGs by taking the difference of extracellular potentials between two points in an isotropic bath surrounding the hearts.
Place the two points near the base of the heart separated by 18 cm.
Ensure the line connecting these two points is perpendicular to the base-apex plane of the septum.
Compute the MAD metric using the formula where X is the ECG waveform of the simulation with estimated fiber orientations.
Use Y as the ECG waveform of the corresponding simulation with acquired fiber orientations.
Calculate X as the mean value of X.
Calculate Y as the mean value of Y.
Determine n as the length of X and Y.
